A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynaGuide research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across the expanded appendix and inserted checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original CALVIN simulations, BlockTouch experiments, and real-robot cup and mouse manipulation results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons and a dynamics-training-data ablation in Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the specified stochastic-sampling update. v1 repeatedly assigns a^(k-1) without updating a^k inside the inner loop; v2 updates a^k for intermediate repetitions and assigns a^(k-1) on the final repetition. This is a limited pseudocode correction; the architecture, objectives, and guidance metric are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CALVIN environments, BlockTouch scenarios, and real-robot CupPreference, HiddenCup, and NovelBehavior tasks. The added comparisons reuse existing data and task coverage; changes in which models receive particular training subsets are experimental controls.

E2.justification: v2 adds hindsight-replay goal conditioning for UnderspecifiedObjectives and classifier-free guidance for MultiObjectives. It also adds DynaGuide-Sampling to the real-robot GuideRed comparison, where v1 compared only guided and base policies. These substantially strengthen comparator coverage in the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Added controls train goal conditioning on all CALVIN environments and train the dynamics model on the target environment alone. Additional baselines sample intermediate future goals or mask goal conditions during training. These extend training and control protocols within existing experiments; the original evaluation metrics and rollout settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a dynamics-training-data ablation comparing CALVIN-D-only training with all-environment training across eight articulated behaviors (Table 5). The existing hyperparameter sweeps, noise-pretraining ablation, and BlockTouch case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions describe simulation uncertainty using one-sigma standard errors from six policy/split evaluations, and 20 real-robot trials without uncertainty intervals (Appendices B.4–B.5). The added tables report further uncertainty values without introducing a new estimation procedure or stating an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Original Figures 4–9 retain their results, while Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6 add substantial comparison and ablation results. Examples include 60% red-cup success for the added sampling baseline versus retained 75% for DynaGuide and 55% for the base policy; switch-on success of 0.54 with target-environment-only dynamics versus 0.74 with all-environment training; and 11–17% no-behavior rates for CFG under negative guidance.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 and Appendix B.3's Gaussian-latent and log-sum-exp derivation are retained. The added discussion of prediction horizons explains practical design tradeoffs without changing formal assumptions, derivations, or mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about modular inference-time steering, multiple positive and negative objectives, robustness, and underrepresented behaviors. The headline 70% articulated-task success and 5.4-fold goal-conditioning comparison are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of cross-environment knowledge transfer (A.4), attributes CFG failures to conflicting, equally weighted guidance signals (A.5), and discusses the tradeoff between predicting final states and fixed-horizon future states (B.3). The main limitations section is retained.

D1.justification: v2 replaces broad tuning ranges with task-specific guidance settings in Table 4, discloses 10-step DDIM inference, specifies a 48-step real-robot prediction horizon and trajectory-based guidance examples, and documents CFG goal masking. These improve implementation disclosure without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Hardware, training budgets, and promised code-release status remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds three cited works: bidirectional decoding, latent-space reinforcement-learning steering, and VLM-in-the-loop steering. Related work incorporates their sampling, initial-noise steering, and VLM-feedback approaches, while retaining the existing positioning of DynaGuide.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in related work, baseline descriptions, and implementation discussion. Appendix A gains dedicated baseline subsections, the old ablation subsection becomes A.4, and a NeurIPS checklist is inserted. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The appendix gains four quantitative comparison/ablation tables and a task-specific hyperparameter table, substantially expanding its evidence displays. Table 6 highlights desired outcomes and failures with color. Algorithm 1's display expands, and retained Figures 8–9 move within the appendix; the original figure graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1's central robustness comparison gave goal conditioning less training-data coverage than DynaGuide's dynamics model. v2 directly tests a goal-conditioned policy with the same broader data, adds hindsight and CFG comparisons, and measures dependence on dynamics training data. These controls substantially strengthen the credibility of the central comparative claims. Corrected pseudocode and more precise implementation details also improve reproducibility, although the small real-robot evaluations still lack uncertainty intervals.
